questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of music videos and how they changed pop music
How to write a sad song that makes listeners cry
A possible biological reason some people enjoy sad music
Why people cry at films more often than at concerts
questions.why: Sam says there might be a biological reason why some of us like sad songs.

questions.q: When did Neil use to listen to sad songs?
options: After breaking up with a girlfriend
When he was studying for exams
When he felt ill
On long car journeys
questions.why: He says he'd listen to sad songs after a break-up, songs which reflected his mood.

questions.q: What was Professor Huron's research trying to find out?
options: Which sad songs are the most popular
Why people love or can't stand sad music
Whether music can make people cry
How music affects babies
questions.why: He wanted to know the difference between people who love sad music and those who can't stand it.

questions.q: Which hormone did the research point towards?
options: Adrenaline
Melatonin
Dopamine
Prolactin
questions.why: He says the research started pointing towards a hormone called prolactin.

questions.q: When, according to Professor Huron, is prolactin also released?
options: When people cry
When people laugh
When people sleep
When people exercise
questions.why: He says, 'When people cry, they also release prolactin.'

options: It makes people more energetic
It makes people angry
It can make people feel comforted
It helps people remember songs
questions.why: He says in some circumstances prolactin seems to have a comforting effect.

questions.q: What does Professor Huron suggest about people who don't like sad music?
options: They produce too much prolactin
They don't listen carefully enough
They prefer happy music for cultural reasons
They may not get enough prolactin when they listen
questions.why: He says maybe they're not getting enough prolactin when they listen to the music.

questions.q: What does Neil find strange about the idea?
options: That sad music is becoming more popular with young people
That feelings are caused by chemicals in the body
That scientists spend money studying music at all
That men and women react so differently to songs
questions.why: He says it's weird to think our feelings are caused by natural chemicals in the body.
